tools.name: get_account_overview
tools.description: Read the current VolunteerReminder account: organization name, plan and entitlements, current reminder send mode, and volunteer usage vs the plan limit. Call this first to understand what the account can do before creating schedules or contacts. Note the `reminder_mode`: an account created through t

tools.name: list_schedules
tools.description: List all active (non-archived) schedules on the account, each with its description, job/role, next upcoming occurrence, and how many volunteers are rostered. Requires the `read` scope.

tools.name: get_schedule
tools.description: Get one schedule's full configuration: recurrence settings, job/role, group, roster (contact ids), start/end dates, and notes. Requires the `read` scope.

tools.name: preview_schedule_occurrences
tools.description: PURE and side-effect-free: computes the next occurrence dates a recurrence configuration WOULD produce, without creating anything. Use this to show the user the concrete dates (e.g. 'the next 8 Tuesdays at 9:00 AM Central') and get their confirmation BEFORE calling create_schedule. Requires the `rea

tools.name: get_upcoming_shifts
tools.description: List a schedule's upcoming occurrences (shifts) in a date range, each with its date/time, whether the roster is attending that date, and the assigned volunteers. Requires the `read` scope.

tools.name: create_schedule
tools.description: Create a recurring (or custom-date) schedule and materialize its upcoming occurrences. Best practice: call preview_schedule_occurrences with the same recurrence settings first and confirm the dates with the user. This tool returns the created schedule AND an inline preview of its next occurrences so

tools.name: update_schedule
tools.description: Partially update a schedule — send only the fields you want to change; unset fields keep their current value. Changing recurrence fields recomputes and re-materializes future occurrences. This tool does NOT change the roster; use assign_contacts_to_schedule for that. Requires the `schedules:write` s

tools.name: archive_schedule
tools.description: Archive (soft-delete) a schedule. It stops appearing in the active list and no further reminders go out for it, but past reminder history is preserved. This is reversible only from the dashboard. Confirm with the user before archiving. Requires the `schedules:write` scope.

tools.name: list_contacts
tools.description: List all volunteers on the account's roster, each with contact details and group. Requires the `read` scope.

tools.name: add_contacts
tools.description: Add one or more volunteers to the roster in a single call. ALL-OR-NOTHING: if the batch would push the account past its plan's volunteer limit, or any contact references a group_id not on this account, NOTHING is added and the error names the limit/count/bad id so you can adjust. Phone numbers are v

tools.name: update_contact
tools.description: Update a volunteer's details. Send only the fields you want to change; a field set to null clears it. Requires the `contacts:write` scope.

tools.name: remove_contact
tools.description: Remove (soft-delete) a volunteer from the roster. This frees a volunteer-cap slot and removes them from any schedule rosters they were on. Confirm with the user before removing. Requires the `contacts:write` scope.

tools.name: assign_contacts_to_schedule
tools.description: Assign volunteers to a schedule. This REPLACES the schedule's entire roster — send the COMPLETE desired set of contact ids, not a delta (pass an empty array to clear it). Every id must belong to this account or the whole request is rejected with the offending ids named. Does not change occurrences.

tools.name: import_volunteer_schedule
tools.description: Parse a pasted or uploaded volunteer roster + schedule (CSV or a table with columns like name, phone, email, job/role, day, start, end) and either PREVIEW or CREATE the contacts, schedules, and assignments. Always call first with confirm=false and show the user the upcoming shifts; only call again w

tools.name: get_open_days
tools.description: List calendar days in the look-ahead window that have no attendable shift yet, plus recurring monthly slots not yet claimed by a schedule — i.e. where the account still needs volunteers. Requires the `read` scope.

tools.name: get_reminder_settings
tools.description: Read the account's reminder lead times (the account-wide default plus any per-job overrides) and which channels (email / SMS) are available on the current plan. Reminder overrides are per JOB, not per individual schedule. Requires the `read` scope.

tools.name: get_send_history
tools.description: Read recent reminder outcomes — which reminders were sent and which failed — newest first, paginated. Use this to confirm reminders actually went out. Requires the `read` scope.

tools.name: set_reminder_rule
tools.description: Set the reminder lead time: the account-wide default and/or a per-job override. Provide at least one of `global_default` or `job_override`, and set at least one of days/hours/minutes greater than zero. Overrides are per JOB (a job may back several schedules). Requires the `reminders:write` scope.

tools.name: remove_reminder_rule
tools.description: Remove a reminder lead-time rule. Provide `job_id` to remove that job's override; omit it to clear the account-wide default. Returns the updated reminder settings. Requires the `reminders:write` scope.

tools.name: send_test_reminder
tools.description: Send a single TEST reminder to the account owner's own email/phone so they can preview what a reminder looks like. This never reaches volunteers — it always reroutes to the owner. Optionally pass a schedule_id to preview that schedule's reminder; otherwise a generic sample is sent. Requires the `rem

tools.name: get_pricing
tools.description: Read VolunteerReminder's public plan catalog: each plan's monthly and annual price (USD), volunteer limit, and included features (SMS reminders are included with no per-message credits or metering). No API key required — use this to help a user comparison-shop or decide which plan fits before they s

tools.description: Start a new VolunteerReminder account for a human, using their email address. findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "preview_schedule_occurrences" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: PURE and side-effect-free: computes the next occurrence dates a recurrence configuration WOULD produce, without creating anything. Use this to show the user the…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "import_volunteer_schedule" stacks urgency/override words (always, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: import_volunteer_schedule, get_reminder_settings, get_pricing, create_account, start_checkout · Private data: get_account_overview, get_schedule, list_contacts, add_contacts, update_contact, remove_contact, assign_contacts_to_schedule, import_volunteer_schedule, get_pricing, create_account, start_checkout · Public sink: get_account_overview, update_schedule, update_contact, assign_contacts_to_schedule, import_volunteer_schedule, get_reminder_settings, get_send_history, send_test_reminder, get_pricing, create_account · Destructive: archive_schedule, remove_contact, remove_reminder_rule.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: import_volunteer_schedule, get_reminder_settings, get_pricing, create_account, start_checkout · Private data: get_account_overview, get_schedule, list_contacts, add_contacts, update_contact, remove_contact, assign_contacts_to_schedule, import_volunteer_schedule, get_pricing, create_account, start_checkout · Public sink: get_account_overview, update_schedule, update_contact, assign_contacts_to_schedule, import_volunteer_schedule, get_reminder_settings, get_send_history, send_test_reminder, get_pricing, create_account · Destructive: archive_schedule, remove_contact, remove_reminder_rule

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
